note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Vine mesquite is a warm-season creeping perennial. Trace ONE continuous aboveground runner to a swollen pubescent node and onward to a leafy flowering shoot; do not infer actual adventitious roots from a merely hairy culm joint. On that same plant seek short appressed flowering branches with smooth oval spikelets. Existing panels show the head and stem but not a proven rooted node.
tiles.short: Follow a vine-like stolon to a swollen hairy node; then inspect a narrow blunt-spikelet head
tiles.status: FIELD-READY GROSS CUE; NEEDS SAME-PLANT ROOTED NODE

tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK THE TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details: Unfold the blade from its sheath and photograph the free inner membrane at 10–20× beside a 1-mm ruler. Published descriptions give an approximately 1–2 mm eciliate membranous ligule. The eighth teaching panel (zero-based index 7, Bob Harms PAOB-L) shows the collar region, but not a calibrated free membrane; nearby sheath or node hairs cannot be measured as the ligule.
tiles.short: Inner ligule ~1–2 mm: eciliate membrane, not the runner-node hairs

tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW THE FLOWERING BRANCHES
tiles.details: Follow the flowering axis rather than judging a detached cluster. Kew reports 1–4 short appressed racemes (~1–2 cm) along a central axis ~3–10(–14) cm; a historical treatment reports 2–6 branches. Count attached branches and photograph the full axis; branch number alone is not a rigid exclusion test. The existing Central Texas flowering panels illustrate real heads, not exact measurements.
tiles.short: Usually 1–4 short appressed racemes ~1–2 cm; published counts vary

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE THE TWO GLUMES
tiles.details: Select five ripe oblong-to-obovate blunt spikelets at 10–20× with a 1-mm scale. Kew gives ~3.4–4 mm; other treatments give ~2.8–4.4 mm. Separate the lower glume (Kew ~0.9–1 spikelet length, 5 veins; older account ~3/4 length, 5–7 veins) from the upper glume (about spikelet length, 7 veins). Do not arrow venation on the current undissected head photos. The linked flowering-unit photograph (zero-based panel 5) shows real attached oval spikelets, NOT separated or measured glumes; no glume-vein arrows are justified.
tiles.short: Mature oval spikelet ~3.4–4 mm; lower glume ~5-veined, upper ~7-veined

tiles.heading: 05 · IDENTIFY BOTH FLORETS
tiles.details: Inside a mature two-flowered spikelet expose the lower staminate lemma with palea (published about spikelet-length and seven-veined), then the hard, finely reticulate, blunt upper fertile lemma (~3.4–4 mm in Kew). Distinguish a lemma from an upper glume before adding labels. A long projecting lemma awn is absent; no existing photograph resolves all parts for accurate arrows. The existing flower close-up is NOT a dissection of the staminate and fertile florets, so this anatomy step deliberately has no diagnostic photo link.
tiles.short: Lower staminate floret; hard shiny reticulate upper fertile lemma, no long awn
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SEPARATE STAMINATE AND FERTILE PARTS

tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT BERMUDAGRASS
tiles.details: Bermudagrass (Cynodon dactylon) also runs aboveground, but commonly bears several slender digitately arranged one-sided branches from nearly one point, with a very short hair-fringed ligule. Switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) has a taller upright habit and large open panicle; buffalograss (Bouteloua dactyloides) is low and dioecious. Require connected runner, attached flowering head and mature spikelets before a confident vine mesquite ID. IMPORTANT: all eight current gallery panels are source-identified Hopia; none is an actual Cynodon, Panicum virgatum or Bouteloua dactyloides look-alike photograph. Leave comparison links empty until properly licensed different-species panels exist.
tiles.short: Hopia's short appressed branches and blunt ovals ≠ Cynodon's radiating fingers
tiles.status: FIELD-READY WRITTEN COMPARISON; NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — TRUE LOOK-ALIKE PANELS

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: FIRST trace the long aboveground vine-like stolon to a SWOLLEN, hairy node with actual roots and young shoot (if visible) on the same live plant. THEN verify the contracted narrow seedhead of rounded, blunt spikelets. The four new Harms source photographs show reproductive branches, stem and collar but NOT one verified connected root-to-seed voucher. Compare Cynodon terminal fingers; do not call a node 'rooted' from a merely hairy stem macro.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START with the source-identified Central Texas flowering panicle (Bob Harms photo i, panel 5); follow attached branches and blunt spikelets.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Unfold the blade from its sheath and photograph the free inner membrane at 10–20× beside a 1-mm ruler. Published descriptions give an approximately 1–2 mm eciliate membranous ligule. The eighth teaching panel (zero-based index 7, Bob Harms PAOB-L) shows the collar region, but not a calibrated free membrane; nearby sheath or node hairs cannot be measured as the ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Follow the flowering axis rather than judging a detached cluster. Kew reports 1–4 short appressed racemes (~1–2 cm) along a central axis ~3–10(–14) cm; a historical treatment reports 2–6 branches. Count attached branches and photograph the full axis; branch number alone is not a rigid exclusion test. The existing Central Texas flowering panels illustrate real heads, not exact measurements.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: BERMUDAGRASS (Cynodon dactylon) also creeps by stolons but usually has 3–7 slender DIGITATE one-sided fingers radiating near one point, rather than Hopia's narrow head of short appressed branches with stout blunt OVAL spikelets; its ligule is a short hair-fringed membranous rim. SWITCHGRASS (Panicum virgatum) normally forms taller erect clumps from rhizomes with a large open much-branched panicle, not vine mesquite's long aboveground node-rooting stolons. BUFFALOGRASS (Bouteloua dactyloides) is low sod-forming and dioecious, with contrasting separate male/female flowering structures rather than vine mesquite's oval spikelets. Do not identify from a vegetative patch or seedhead shape alone; trace the node and examine attached spikelets.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: 4 · SECOND LOCAL IMAGE — exact-source CC BY photo

panels.caption: A complementary archive image with a documented photographer and source. The site must not claim that its true rooting nodes or membranous collar are visible without verifying those organs in the original photograph.
panels.why_it_matters: Keep photo source evidence adjacent to morphological teaching while documenting what still needs a closer view.

memory_rule: RUNNER + HAIRY SWOLLEN ROOTING NODE + NARROW, BLUNT OVAL-SPIKELET HEAD = vine mesquite candidate. Bermudagrass's terminal fingers are different. Confirm an intact plant.
safety_note: Six locally archived images and three remote-only source entries. Harms images copyrighted with credited educational permission, not CC. No attached rooted-stolon photograph or calibrated dissected mature spikelet. All eight teaching panels are Hopia, not a photographed side-by-side with Cynodon; panel numbers in this walkthrough are one-based, while field-ID photo_panel_indices are zero-based.
field_rule: Connected rooted runner plus diagnostic slender flowering branches with blunt spikelets; confirm collar from same plant.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
